$comment: CANONICAL MACHINE-READABLE TARGET MODEL — the single source of truth for the target database.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (Workstream I):
The attribute grid, data dictionary, ERD, constraint matrix, PII matrix and index list are all
PROJECTIONS of the same facts. Hand-maintaining them as prose would mean ~600 cells duplicated
across six documents, guaranteed to diverge the first time one column changes. This programme has
already recorded five instances of a check reporting green over a scope that quietly shrank; six
hand-copied views of one model is the documentation equivalent.
So: this file is authored, everything else is GENERATED (scripts/db/generate_model_docs.mjs) and
VALIDATED (scripts/db/validate_target_model.mjs). Never edit a generated document.
NOT EXECUTABLE. This is a specification, not DDL. No migration is generated from it yet.
COLUMN DEFAULTS applied by the generator when a key is omitted:
nullable:false  pk:false  unique:false  generated:null  fk:null  onDelete:null
pii:'NONE'  financial:'NONE'  encryption:'NONE'  retention:'WITH_PARENT'
audit:'CHANGES_AUDITED'  mutable:true  api:'INTERNAL'  conflict:'LAST_WRITE_WINS'
sourceOfTruth:'THIS_TABLE'  legacy:null  legacyPath:null
VOCABULARY (closed sets, enforced by the validator):
pii:        NONE | PSEUDONYMOUS_ID | DIRECT_IDENTIFIER | CONTACT | SENSITIVE_SNAPSHOT
financial:  NONE | MONETARY_AMOUNT | CURRENCY_CODE | EXTERNAL_REFERENCE | DERIVED_MONETARY
encryption: NONE | AT_REST_PROVIDER | COLUMN_LEVEL_REQUIRED
retention:  WITH_PARENT | RETAIN_5Y_FINANCIAL | RETAIN_5Y_AUDIT | RETAIN_24M_AFTER_LAST_USE |
RETAIN_90D_PAYLOAD | REDACT_IN_PLACE | INDEFINITE_REFERENCE
audit:      NOT_AUDITED | CHANGES_AUDITED | APPEND_ONLY | IMMUTABLE_AFTER_INSERT
api:        INTERNAL | VIA_VIEW | VIA_RPC_ONLY | PUBLIC_PROJECTION
mutable:    true | false        (false ⇒ UPDATE forbidden by trigger or policy)
conflict:   LAST_WRITE_WINS | OPTIMISTIC_VERSION | APPEND_ONLY_NO_CONFLICT | OPERATOR_RESOLVES

meta.generatedFor: Ferrarilabs bolão platform — DB modernization target
meta.currencyPolicy: ISO-4217 code stored explicitly per monetary row. USD is the CURRENT value, never an assumption baked into the schema. No DEFAULT on currency columns that carry unknown historical amounts.
meta.moneyType: numeric(14,2) — exact decimal. FLOAT/REAL/DOUBLE are prohibited platform-wide.

schemas.bolao: Base tables. NOT exposed to PostgREST.
schemas.bolao_api: security_invoker views + RPCs. The only public surface.
schemas.audit: audit_events and its sensitive-detail sidecar. Not exposed.
schemas.public: legacy only (bolao_state, lottery_*) during migration; retired after cutover.

meta.enumsRationale: Enum TYPES were referenced by 14 columns but their VALUES were never declared anywhere — a gap found while generating the M1 migration draft, which cannot create a type it has no values for. Values are taken from the executable modules that already own each vocabulary (financial.mjs, outbox.mjs, identity.mjs) so the SQL and the JS cannot drift apart.

entities.name: participants
entities.purpose: A durable person who takes part in pools, across competitions and years. PII lives here and ONLY here.
entities.rollbackImplication: Dropping loses the identity graph; participant_identity_links must be dropped first (FK).

columns.notes: Surrogate. Never derived from PII.

columns.backfill: one participant per historical entry; ZERO merges on first pass

columns.notes: Nullable by evidence — many historical entries have none. Uniqueness is partial, never a merge trigger.
RETAIN ONLY IF A PURPOSE IS CONFIRMED — data minimisation (DATA_GOVERNANCE G-01). Currently no identified use.
NULL ⇒ this row IS canonical. Non-NULL ⇒ superseded by a merge; see participant_identity_links.
Maintained by trigger, not by the application — bolao_state's updated_at was app-maintained and therefore unreliable.
Erasure-by-redaction (G-02). Row and FKs survive; PII columns are nulled.

indexes.partial: email IS NOT NULL AND redacted_at IS NULL
indexes.rationale: dedup candidate lookup; partial because email is nullable and redacted rows must not block reuse
resolve a superseded identity to its canonical row; unindexed FK would full-scan
candidate-match workflow searches by name; expression index avoids a scan

KPLUS-OP-2, added on measured workload evidence and on nothing else. Without this index PostgreSQL's referential-integrity check on a parent delete or key update reads 15,000 rows at TIER_100X and the count tracks the table; with it the check examines only rows that match. Twelve other unindexed foreign keys were measured the same way and deliberately NOT indexed — for ten the planner declines the index even when it exists. Evidence: fingerprints/P_performance_baseline.json.

checks.name: participants_canonical_not_self
checks.expr: canonical_participant_id IS NULL OR canonical_participant_id <> participant_id
checks.why: a row cannot supersede itself — would create a 1-cycle

checks.name: participants_redaction_complete
checks.expr: redacted_at IS NULL OR (display_name IS NULL AND email IS NULL AND phone IS NULL)
checks.why: a redacted row must not retain PII; makes partial redaction impossible

checks.name: participants_display_name_present_unless_redacted
checks.expr: display_name IS NOT NULL OR redacted_at IS NOT NULL
checks.why: display_name was NOT NULL, which made participants_redaction_complete unsatisfiable: that check requires display_name IS NULL once redacted_at is set, so no row could ever be redacted at all (KPLUS-F008, found by workstream F against a real server). The column is now nullable and this check carries the original guarantee exactly — every LIVE participant still must have a name, and NULL is reachable only in the redacted state the model already describes.

entities.name: participant_identity_links
entities.purpose: Audited, REVERSIBLE record of every identity merge. Over-merging money is unrecoverable, so the merge itself must be an undoable, attributable act.
entities.rollbackImplication: Dropping loses merge provenance — the merges themselves would become irreversible. Never drop without exporting.

columns.notes: RESTRICT deliberately: deleting a participant that absorbed another would orphan the provenance.
The row that was superseded. RETAINED, never deleted — that is what makes the merge reversible.
What the candidate-match workflow found. MUST NOT contain raw email/name — store field NAMES and match kinds, not values (B1).

columns.validation: non-empty; an unexplained merge is not acceptable

columns.notes: RESTRICT: an unattributable merge is worse than no record.

indexes.rationale: a participant may be actively merged into at most ONE survivor; partial so a reverted merge frees it for re-merge
list everything absorbed by a canonical participant

checks.name: pil_no_self_merge
checks.expr: surviving_participant_id <> merged_participant_id
checks.why: merging a row into itself is meaningless and creates a cycle

checks.name: pil_revert_complete
checks.expr: (reverted_at IS NULL) = (reverted_by IS NULL)
checks.why: a revert without an actor is unattributable

checks.name: pil_reason_present
checks.expr: length(btrim(reason)) > 0
checks.why: every merge must carry a written justification

entities.name: participant_auth_links
entities.purpose: Which auth identities own which participants. KPLUS-F047: this table is RATIFIED (WS12-OP-2), every ownership policy in the RLS model queries it, and write_contracts authorizes against it ('caller owns pool_entry_id via participant_auth_links') — and it was in no model entry and no migration phase. The RLS draft shipped it as a COMMENTED-OUT prerequisite, so applying the migration as generated would have left every ownership policy referencing a relation that does not exist. Found by NIGHT-1, the first run to apply RLS to a database built from zero.
entities.rollbackImplication: Dropping it breaks every ownership policy — authenticated users lose access to their own rows. Fully rebuildable from the auth provider, but not while policies reference it.

columns.notes: Composite PK with auth_user_id: identity and participant are DIFFERENT things. One user may own several participants, and a historical participant may have no auth row at all — which is why ownership is a link table and not a column comparison on participants.
RESTRICT, not CASCADE: silently dropping a link would silently revoke a participant's access to their own data.
When the link was established. Immutable — a re-link is a new row, not an edit.

entities.rollbackImplication: Reference data; safe to drop only if no editions exist.

entities.rollbackImplication: Dropping cascades conceptually to pools; use RESTRICT so it cannot be dropped while pools exist.

columns.notes: e.g. '2026'. Text not integer: some competitions span two calendar years ('2026/27').
Numeric handle for year-over-year reporting; season_label stays the display form.

indexes.rationale: one edition per competition per season; also the year-over-year join key

checks.name: ce_dates_ordered
checks.expr: starts_on IS NULL OR ends_on IS NULL OR starts_on <= ends_on
checks.why: an edition cannot end before it starts

entities.name: competition_edition_phases
entities.purpose: A phase within an edition (oitavas, quartas, …) carrying its own entry cutoff. Gives the deadline exactly ONE home, closing J-05's two-sources-of-cutoff problem.
entities.rollbackImplication: Ties reference phases; RESTRICT.

columns.notes: Phase sequence. Drives the valid-transition check in the data-quality framework.
Deadlines gate money; this is the authoritative copy. CONFIG.cutoffIso becomes a deploy-time default only.

columns.backfill: READ FROM THE LIVE DOCUMENT, not from emptyPhaseState() — this key exists only post-merge and was already silently dropped once (J-06).

columns.notes: Bracket topology + provenance. Document-shaped by nature; stays JSONB as a column on a relational row.
columns.sourceEvidence: NO LIVE SOURCE. This column was declared with legacyPath 'phases{}.topology', a key none of the three production documents carries — measured 2026-08-12 across all nine cdb2026 phases and both single-phase products. The key the documents DO carry, officialDraw, now has its own column (M15-F2). `topology` therefore has no backfill source today and stays NULL until a document actually grows one; it is not a gap, it is an unused target.

columns.notes: Mirrors the existing DRAW_LIFECYCLE derivation. DERIVED in the app today; stored here only as a materialised convenience, never as the source of truth.

columns.purpose: The official draw record for this phase: the event that fixed its bracket, with its authority, sources, corroboration, hashes and validation stamps. Kept as its own column and NOT folded into `topology`, which is declared for bracket TOPOLOGY — a draw event and a bracket shape are different facts, and `draw_state` is explicitly DERIVED from this one, so hiding it inside a differently-named column is what produced M15-F2 in the first place.
columns.sourceEvidence: bolao_state['cdb2026'].phases{}.officialDraw. Measured 2026-08-12: present on `quartas` only, carrying authority, event, source, sourceUrl, corroboratedBy, bracketHash, ingestedAt, scheduledAt, validatedAt, validatedBy and note. Consumed by enforceDrawLifecycle() in bolao/cdb2026/js/app.js, which wipes a gated phase's ties unless officialDraw.validatedAt is present — so this object currently gates whether a phase's ties are shown at all.
columns.nullSemantics: NULL means no official draw has been recorded for that phase. Eight of cdb2026's nine phases are in that state, and it is not the same as an empty draw: a phase with no draw is gated shut, a phase with an empty one would claim a draw happened and produced nothing.
columns.noDefault: deliberately no DEFAULT. An empty object would assert that a draw occurred.

indexes.rationale: one phase per slug per edition
phase order must be unambiguous for transition validation

entities.name: classification_snapshots
entities.purpose: One retrieval of a league classification for a competition edition. The ENVELOPE only: who provided it, when, whether it is stale, and whether a later correction supersedes it. The club rows live in competition_edition_standings. Modelled because br2026 scoring consumes the league table and no existing entity can hold it: match_results requires goals, ranking_snapshots is keyed on pool_entry_id (a participant, not a club), and ties/matches are knockout pairings.

rlsIntent.anon: select via public projection — a league table is public information already published by the provider

entities.rollbackImplication: FULL before any snapshot is imported. After import, FORWARD_FIX_ONLY: a snapshot is provider evidence retrieved at a moment that cannot be re-retrieved, and the zone boundaries a past round's scoring was computed against are exactly this row.

columns.notes: A classification is meaningless without its edition: position 1 of which season.
Evidence: the snapshot envelope's `provider` field, currently always 'espn'.
Evidence: the envelope's `competitionId`, e.g. 'bra.1'. Kept so a snapshot can be traced back to the exact feed it came from.
Evidence: sync_espn.py's STANDINGS_CONFIG.source_url.
Evidence: the envelope's `schemaVersion`. Stored so a shape change is a data fact rather than a silent reinterpretation.
Evidence: `generatedAt`. The instant the provider snapshot was produced; this is what orders snapshots.
Evidence: `sourceUpdatedAt`. May lag generated_at when the provider served a cached response.
Evidence: `payloadHash`. NOT unique: the cron re-runs on an unchanged table and an identical payload at a later instant is a legitimate second snapshot.
Evidence: the envelope's `stale`. A stale snapshot means the fetch failed and the last known good data was reused. It must never be authoritative.
Evidence: `staleReason`. Required whenever is_stale, enforced by a CHECK: a snapshot that cannot say why it is stale cannot be triaged.

How many standing rows this snapshot carries. Stored so a TRUNCATED import is refusable: the zone boundaries are position slices, so nineteen rows instead of twenty silently moves the relegation zone.
NULL for the sync runtime, set for an operator correction.

indexes.rationale: the authoritative-snapshot lookup: the latest classification for this edition. The single hottest access path, read once per scoring run.
one snapshot per provider per instant per edition. Two rows claiming the same instant would make 'the latest' ambiguous.

checks.name: classification_snapshots_club_count_positive
checks.expr: club_count > 0
checks.why: an empty classification is not a classification

checks.name: classification_snapshots_stale_has_reason
checks.expr: is_stale IS FALSE OR stale_reason IS NOT NULL
checks.why: a stale snapshot must say why, or it cannot be triaged

entities.notes: A correction needs no supersession POINTER. The authoritative classification for an edition is simply the latest non-stale snapshot by generated_at, and (competition_edition_id, provider, generated_at) is unique — so a corrected import is a new row with a later instant and ordering alone resolves it. An earlier draft copied match_results' superseded_by_id pattern, which would have required an UPDATE and therefore contradicted this table being append-only. match_results needs its flag because several results for one match can legitimately coexist; a classification has exactly one latest.

entities.name: competition_edition_standings
entities.purpose: One club's line in one classification snapshot: its resolved position and its league statistics. This is a LEAGUE TABLE row, not a participant ranking — ranking_snapshots is the participant concept and is keyed on pool_entry_id. br2026's G4/Z4/SA6 zones are pure POSITION SLICES of this table (G4 = 1-4, SA6 = 7-12, Z4 = 17-20), so no zone membership is stored: it is derived from position plus the competition's own rules. Evidence: bolao/br2026/scripts/send_round_email.py:448-450 and bolao/br2026/js/app.js:629-631 (identical slicing in both), plus the persisted snapshot bolao/br2026/data/espn-standings-normalized.json.

rlsIntent.anon: select via public projection — the league table is public information

entities.rollbackImplication: FULL before any snapshot is imported. After import, FORWARD_FIX_ONLY: these rows are what a past round's zone boundaries were computed from.

columns.notes: The edition is reached through the snapshot and is deliberately NOT repeated here: a copy could disagree with its parent about which season it belongs to.

The RESOLVED position, 1..club_count, after the app's own deterministic tiebreak. Materialised so no reader re-derives it; the UNIQUE (snapshot, position) index is the 2026-07-14 zone-boundary audit finding made structural.
The provider's own rank, which CAN TIE — that tie is precisely why `position` exists as a separate resolved value. Kept as evidence of what the provider actually said.

The club identity br2026 scoring compares picks against — the provider's displayName. NOT a foreign key: there is no clubs entity, and inventing a global club master for one competition's league table would be a much larger model change than the evidence supports. The app warns on a name absent from its own DATA.teams list rather than rejecting it.

Provided by the source independently of goals_for/goals_against, so a CHECK asserts the three agree when all are present. A provider that contradicts itself is a CONFLICT the transformer must surface, not silently prefer one field over another.

indexes.rationale: two clubs cannot occupy the same position in one snapshot. This is the 2026-07-14 zone-boundary audit finding enforced by the database: an unresolved provider rank tie now fails the import instead of moving a relegation boundary.
a club cannot occupy two positions in one snapshot
the scoring read: fetch a snapshot's table in position order and slice the zones. Covering, so the zone slice needs no heap access.

checks.name: competition_edition_standings_position_positive
checks.expr: position > 0
checks.why: position is 1-based; a zero or negative position would shift every zone slice

checks.name: competition_edition_standings_gd_consistent
checks.expr: goals_for IS NULL OR goals_against IS NULL OR goal_difference IS NULL OR goal_difference = goals_for - goals_against
checks.why: the source supplies goal difference independently of the goal counts; if they disagree the row is not trustworthy and must be refused rather than reconciled by guesswork

checks.name: competition_edition_standings_counts_non_negative
checks.expr: (played IS NULL OR played >= 0) AND (wins IS NULL OR wins >= 0) AND (draws IS NULL OR draws >= 0) AND (losses IS NULL OR losses >= 0) AND (goals_for IS NULL OR goals_for >= 0) AND (goals_against IS NULL OR goals_against >= 0)
checks.why: a negative match or goal count is impossible and would indicate a parse error

entities.name: pools
entities.purpose: A betting pool for one edition. The money boundary: fees, prize split and entries all hang off it.
entities.rollbackImplication: Money-bearing children (entries, allocations). RESTRICT everywhere; never cascade.

columns.check: enum: draft | open | closed | settled | archived

columns.validation: values are exact decimals summing to 1.0
columns.notes: AUTHORITATIVE evidence: identical 70/20/10 in all three configs.

columns.purpose: The frozen entry deadline for this pool: the instant after which entries and prediction edits are refused. NOT the edition's schedule — competition_editions.starts_on/ends_on are the competition's dates, and a pool's entry window is a different fact that an edition could host several of.
columns.sourceEvidence: bolao_state['br2026'].cutoffAt. Produced by freezeSeasonCutoff() in bolao/br2026/js/app.js, which computes (first upcoming kickoff - 1 hour) via computeSeasonCutoffIso() and writes it ONCE (`if (s.cutoffAt) return false`). Consumed by cutoffDate() -> isPastCutoff() -> `locked`, which disables the pick selects. It controls write eligibility.
columns.timezoneSemantics: an absolute instant. computeSeasonCutoffIso() ends in Date#toISOString(), so the stored string is always UTC with a Z suffix (measured: 24 characters). timestamptz stores the instant; no timezone meaning is converted or guessed.
columns.nullSemantics: NULL means no frozen cutoff exists for this pool. Two source states map here and the distinction is preserved in lineage, not in the column: KEY_ABSENT (main, cdb2026 — those pools do not use this mechanism at all) and JSON_NULL (the br2026 pre-freeze state, where the app falls back to CONFIG.cutoffIso). Neither is observable in production today: br2026 carries a value and the other two carry nothing.
columns.mutability: write-once by the app, but operator-mutable in practice — config.js records that the production value was extended by 45 minutes directly in Supabase. The column therefore must NOT be made immutable by a trigger.
columns.noDefault: deliberately no DEFAULT. A now() default would fabricate a deadline for every pool that has none, and that deadline would silently decide whether real entries were late.

indexes.rationale: stable public identifier

entities.name: pool_fee_schedule
entities.purpose: The entry fee for a pool, over time. A schedule rather than a column because a pool may be re-priced and history must stay stable.
entities.rollbackImplication: Entries snapshot the fee, so dropping the schedule does not corrupt existing entries — that is the point of the snapshot.

columns.backfill: 5 for all three football pools — AUTHORITATIVE, and verified unchanged across ~40 historical revisions of each config. Powerball is per-cota at 20 (PROBABLE: the figure lives in prose).

columns.notes: NO DEFAULT, NOT NULL — deliberate. U1 ratified CURRENT_POOL_CURRENCY=USD, but a defaulted currency would let a future pool silently inherit USD and produce wrong money. Backfill sets 'USD' explicitly per row.
Football pools are per_entry; Powerball is per_cota. Modelling this avoids forcing one shape onto both.
NULL ⇒ currently in force.
Carries B-08's evidence classification INTO the data. A fee whose provenance is weak is visible as such rather than laundered into a bare number.
e.g. 'versioned_config:CONFIG.entryFee'. Provenance of the value.

indexes.rationale: resolve the fee in force at a point in time
at most ONE currently-in-force fee per pool — prevents two live prices

checks.name: pfs_period_ordered
checks.expr: effective_to IS NULL OR effective_from < effective_to
checks.why: a fee period cannot end before it begins

entities.name: pool_entries
entities.purpose: One competitive entry: this participant, in this pool, with these predictions. Ratified name (E1); replaces 'participation'.

rlsIntent.anon: none (public ranking reads a projection instead)

entities.rollbackImplication: Money-bearing. Allocations and predictions reference it. RESTRICT; soft-delete instead.

columns.backfill: reuse the client-generated uuid verbatim — it is already a stable surrogate

columns.notes: NO unique constraint on (participant_id, pool_id) — multiple entries per participant per pool is a RATIFIED requirement. This deliberately supersedes M-3.
MANDATORY. With uniqueness on (participant_id, pool_id) removed, this is the only thing distinguishing an intentional second entry from an accidental duplicate.

SNAPSHOT, not a lookup. A 2026 entry keeps its 2026 fee after a 2027 re-price. Deriving from the CURRENT schedule row would silently rewrite history — the single most important modelling decision in the financial domain.
Snapshotted with the amount. NOT NULL, no default — an entry whose currency is unknown cannot be created, forcing the gap into the open.
Which schedule row the snapshot came from. Nullable because legacy entries predate the schedule.
Share count for per_cota pools. 1 for per_entry pools.
NEVER STORED as an authoritative boolean. Derived in bolao_api from allocations vs expected fee. Values: unpaid | partially_paid | settled | overpaid | legacy_asserted.

columns.backfill: tombstone set → per-row soft delete. RETIRE deletedIds LAST, only after writes are server-mediated.

checks.expr: length(btrim(entry_label)) > 0
checks.why: the only discriminator between deliberate and accidental duplicates

entities.name: payments
entities.purpose: An inbound money movement as it actually happened. Deliberately NOT tied to a single entry — a payer may fund several.
entities.rollbackImplication: Financial record. NEVER cascade-delete. Reversal is modelled, not deletion.

columns.notes: THIS IS HOW payer ≠ participant IS EXPRESSED. Nullable only for legacy rows where the payer is unrecoverable.
NULLABLE ONLY for legacy_asserted rows migrated from the paid boolean, where no amount ever existed. A NULL amount can never be allocated.

columns.check: enum: contribution | adjustment | refund | reversal | chargeback | void

columns.notes: zelle | venmo | cashapp | pix | paypal | other
Carries forward the ONE genuinely enforced constraint in the current schema. MUST NOT appear in any report or public view — the txId governance rule.
Self-reference. A reversal points at what it reverses; neither row is ever deleted.
Free text — treat as potentially PII-bearing and keep out of reports.
amount − SUM(allocations). DERIVED, never stored: a stored balance is a second truth that drifts. See FINANCIAL_MODEL reconciliation equations.

indexes.rationale: makes double-recording a payment reference impossible; observed firing 11/11 on inserts in production
'everything this person paid' — the payment-history report
find the reversal of a payment without scanning

checks.name: pay_no_self_reverse
checks.expr: reverses_payment_id IS NULL OR reverses_payment_id <> payment_id
checks.why: a payment cannot reverse itself

checks.name: pay_amount_currency_together
checks.expr: (amount IS NULL) = (currency IS NULL)
checks.why: an amount without a currency is not money

entities.name: payment_allocations
entities.purpose: Applies part of a payment to a specific entry. Resolves the real many-to-many: one payment may fund several entries; one entry may be funded by several payments.
entities.rollbackImplication: Deleting an allocation silently changes settlement. Prefer a compensating negative allocation over deletion.

columns.notes: MUST equal the payment's currency AND the entry's expected_fee_currency. Cross-currency allocation is a data-quality violation, not a feature.

indexes.rationale: sum allocations per entry — the settlement derivation; the single most important index in the financial domain
one allocation row per (payment, entry) pair; adjust by amending the row, not by adding a second

entities.name: prize_allocations
entities.purpose: OUTBOUND money: a prize awarded to an entry. Kept strictly separate from entry payments — conflating inbound and outbound makes reconciliation ambiguous.
entities.rollbackImplication: Financial record; never cascade.

columns.notes: Denormalised from the entry for reporting. Kept consistent by a data-quality rule, not by trust.
e.g. 0.70000. Lets a prize be split across multiple entries on the same rank.

indexes.rationale: 'everything this person won' — the winnings report
prize per entry
an entry cannot be awarded the same rank twice, while a rank may still be split across entries

checks.name: prz_net_le_gross
checks.expr: net_amount IS NULL OR net_amount <= gross_amount
checks.why: net cannot exceed gross

entities.name: ties
entities.purpose: A two-legged knockout tie. CONTAINS matches and carries aggregate/qualification rules — a tie is NOT a match, and collapsing them would lose the aggregate.
entities.rollbackImplication: Matches and predictions reference ties; RESTRICT.

columns.notes: Which side advanced. NOT a pairing input — see the draw-provenance invariant: nothing may derive a pairing from qualified teams.
Official-draw provenance (authority, source, validatedAt, bracketHash). Preserved verbatim from the existing model — it is what makes the bracket auditable.
Bracket progression QF→SF→Final.

columns.purpose: When this tie was frozen by an operator. Operator-action provenance on a result-bearing object: after a tie is locked its picks can no longer be edited, so this is the instant that decided which predictions counted.
columns.sourceEvidence: bolao_state['cdb2026'].phases{}.ties{}.lockedAt. Measured 2026-08-12: present on 8 of 28 ties. Found by PRODMIG-M15-F4.
columns.timezoneSemantics: an absolute instant, stored as timestamptz. The source strings are ISO-8601 with a Z suffix.
columns.nullSemantics: NULL means the tie was never locked. That is the ordinary state for 20 of the 28 ties and must not be confused with 'locked at an unknown time'.
columns.noDefault: deliberately no DEFAULT. A now() default would record every unlocked tie as having been locked at migration time — a fabricated operator action.
columns.mutability: written once when an operator locks the tie. Not immutable by trigger: an operator may unlock, and forcing immutability here would make a legitimate correction impossible.

KPLUS-F032. NULL means the snapshot is a draft and is visible to no browser principal; a timestamp publishes it. The RLS model has gated anon and authenticated reads on this column since it was written (published_at IS NOT NULL) and the column did not exist, so CREATE POLICY refused it and the entire RLS draft aborted at that statement — every policy and every table privilege after it never ran. The column is added rather than the predicate relaxed: relaxing it would make every computed ranking world-readable the moment it is written, which is a visibility decision the model never took, and it required deleting a mutation-tested security assertion to pass. Distinct from is_provisional, which is a PRESENTATION contract (a provisional standing is shown, labelled as a projection) and not an access-control one.

entities.name: audit_chain_head
entities.purpose: The current tail of the audit hash chain, as a single row. Exists so that appending an event is O(1): without it the trigger has to find the one event nothing points back to, which is a scan of the whole audit log on every insert and makes bulk insertion quadratic (measured — a 200,000-row load did not finish). Locking this row FOR UPDATE also gives the serialisation the chain needs, so concurrent writers are ordered rather than failed. See ADR-K01.

rlsIntent.service: none — maintained only by the audit trigger

entities.rollbackImplication: Dropping it disables audit appends entirely; it is rebuildable from audit_events by walking to the open end.

columns.notes: Always true. With the CHECK below this makes a second row impossible, so 'the chain head' can never become ambiguous.
NULL before the first event exists. Never chosen by a caller.
Independent count of chain links, so a verifier can detect events removed behind the triggers without walking the whole chain.

checks.name: audit_chain_head_singleton
checks.expr: singleton
checks.why: one chain, one head; a second row would make the tail ambiguous and permit two parallel chains

entities.name: audit_events
entities.purpose: Append-only, hash-chained record of what a human did. B1-compliant: identifiers, not PII.
entities.rollbackImplication: APPEND-ONLY. Never dropped, never updated. Rollback of a migration must not delete audit rows.

columns.notes: RESTRICT: deleting a user must not orphan the audit trail. ID only — NEVER an email snapshot (that is what B1 prohibits).
aggregate.past_tense, e.g. pool_entry.created
Polymorphic by design — no FK is possible. A data-quality rule checks resolvability instead.
Groups every event of one logical operation, across audit and outbox.
IDs, enum values, counts, amounts. MUST NOT contain names, emails, phones, payment references or large payloads (B1). A data-quality rule scans for shapes that look like PII.
Computed by a BEFORE INSERT trigger over the NON-PII columns only. Excluding the sidecar is what lets PII be redacted without breaking the chain (G-02).

indexes.rationale: 'what happened to this object' — the audit lookup path, currently a full scan in the legacy table
chronological audit reads

KPLUS-F013(b). At most ONE event may follow any given event. This makes a forked hash chain structurally impossible rather than merely unlikely: two concurrent inserts that both read the same tail cannot both commit, because the second violates this index. The chain-building trigger also serialises on an advisory lock, so this is the second of two independent defences — the one that still holds if the first is ever removed. Partial because the genesis event has no predecessor.
KPLUS-F013(b). The chain is walked by matching previous_event_hash to event_hash, which is only unambiguous if event_hash identifies exactly one row. Also the lookup path for chain verification.
reconstruct one logical operation end to end

KPLUS-OP-2, added on measured workload evidence and on nothing else. Without this index PostgreSQL's referential-integrity check on a parent delete or key update reads 200,000 rows at TIER_100X and the count tracks the table; with it the check examines only rows that match. Twelve other unindexed foreign keys were measured the same way and deliberately NOT indexed — for ten the planner declines the index even when it exists. Evidence: fingerprints/P_performance_baseline.json.

columns.notes: Redaction here does NOT break audit_events.event_hash — by design.

dedupe — the single most important constraint in this domain

checks.why: an attempt cannot finish before it starts

entities.name: request_idempotency
entities.purpose: Exactly-once effect for server-mediated writes. All nine write contracts specify an idempotency lookup and record; until this table existed there was nowhere to put one, so every retry was a possible double-write (KPLUS-F018). The record is written INSIDE the business transaction: before it, a crash marks a request done that never happened; after it, a retry doubles the write.
entities.rollbackImplication: FULL while empty. Once it holds money-bearing records, FORWARD_FIX_ONLY: dropping it converts every in-flight retry into a potential double payment.

columns.notes: The write contract name. Part of the key, so the same client key in two contracts is two independent requests.
Client-supplied. One of the few values a client legitimately controls; it names the request, never its effect.

sha256 hex over the canonicalised payload with sorted keys, excluding request_id and correlation_id. Stored, not just compared: telling a retry from a key collision needs the original to compare against.
PII class: SENSITIVE_SNAPSHOT. Replayed verbatim on a matching retry; recomputing it could return a different answer than the call being replayed.
Drives retention. A money-bearing record is never automatically deleted, and a pruned one makes a retry REFUSED rather than executed.
NULL means never automatically prunable. A money-bearing record must have NULL here, enforced by ri_money_never_expires.

indexes.rationale: THE key. Uniqueness lives in the database because check-then-insert races with itself: two concurrent retries both find nothing and both write.
a pruner must find its named set without scanning records it is not allowed to touch

checks.name: ri_money_never_expires
checks.expr: NOT (money_bearing AND prunable_after IS NOT NULL)
checks.why: the choreography forbids automatic deletion of a money-bearing idempotency record; a CHECK makes that something the database will not permit rather than something a pruner has to remember

checks.name: ri_fingerprint_is_sha256
checks.expr: payload_fingerprint ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'
checks.why: a truncated or differently-encoded fingerprint would silently compare unequal and turn every retry into a conflict

entities.name: migration_lineage
entities.purpose: Row-level provenance for every application row a backfill creates. The campaign requires that every target row resolve to a SOURCE or an APPROVED_DERIVATION, and that every source element resolve to a target — and until now there was nowhere in the database to record either direction. PRODMIG-Q25 could not have satisfied its own lineage criterion without this.
entities.rollbackImplication: FULL before any backfill writes lineage. Afterwards this table IS the backout mechanism: a run's rows are identified by migration_run_id, so dropping it would destroy the ability to reverse the backfill it describes.

columns.purpose: The run that created the target row. This is what makes a per-run backout exact: a run's rows are exactly the rows naming it, so cleanup never has to guess and never touches an unrelated row.
Which transformer produced it. Two runs of different versions over the same source can legitimately differ, and without this the difference is unattributable.

TARGET -> SOURCE. Deliberately NOT a foreign key: it points at whichever relation target_relation names, and an FK can only point at one. The reconciliation job checks it instead, which is also what lets lineage outlive a row that a later CONTRACT stage removes.
NULL where the source is not pool-scoped. Powerball is its own domain and does not borrow football pool semantics.
The JSON path or column the value came from, e.g. `state.entries[3].entryLabel`. A PATH, never a VALUE.

A digest of the source element, never the element. It answers 'did the thing I migrated change since?' without storing what it was — which is the only way this table can hold provenance for participant data without becoming a second copy of it.
MIGRATED, DERIVED_WITH_PROOF or APPROVED_EXCLUSION — the same vocabulary the source-element accounting uses, so the two cannot drift into describing different things.

indexes.rationale: the backout path: every row one run created. Without it, reversing a run scans the whole lineage table.
TARGET -> SOURCE: 'where did this row come from', the question an auditor asks about one row.
SOURCE -> TARGET: the direction that finds a source element nothing migrated.

the IDEMPOTENCY key. A retry of the same run over the same source path must be a no-op rather than a second lineage row — and idempotency has to be a supported workflow, not a constraint violation somebody catches.

checks.name: ml_disposition_known
checks.expr: disposition IN ('MIGRATED','DERIVED_WITH_PROOF','APPROVED_EXCLUSION')
checks.why: UNKNOWN is not a disposition a row may carry; an unresolved element blocks its domain instead of being recorded as migrated-ish

checks.name: ml_source_path_present
checks.expr: length(btrim(source_path)) > 0
checks.why: lineage that does not say where a row came from is not lineage

checks.name: ml_fingerprint_present
checks.expr: length(btrim(source_fingerprint)) > 0
checks.why: a fingerprint is what makes the source claim checkable later

entities.name: classification_predictions
entities.purpose: A participant's prediction that a named club finishes in a given ZONE at a given POSITION within that zone. br2026's entries[].picks is {g4:[4], sa6:[6], z4:[4]} — fourteen club-zone assertions per entry, 154 live. It cannot go in bolao.predictions: that table's CHECK pred_subject_exactly_one requires a match_id XOR a tie_id, and a zone pick has neither. It is equally NOT classification_snapshots/competition_edition_standings, which model the PROVIDER's observed league table (points, played, wins) — an observation, not a prediction. A queued task proposed exactly that mapping; the schema refutes it.
entities.rollbackImplication: Dropping loses every zone pick; they are re-derivable from bolao_state[br2026].entries[].picks for as long as legacy is retained.

columns.notes: The zone slug as the application names it: g4, sa6, z4. Validated by SHAPE, not against a value list — a CHECK enumerating those three would freeze br2026's vocabulary into the schema and refuse the next competition's zones, which is a business rule wearing an integrity constraint's clothes.

1-based position WITHIN the zone. LOAD-BEARING, not decorative: bolao/br2026/scripts/audit_scoring.py compares pg4[i] positionally and pays G4_EXACT for the right club in the right position but only G4_GROUP for the right club in the wrong one. Storing these as an unordered set would silently change what every br2026 entry scores.

columns.nullSemantics: NOT NULL, and the EMPTY STRING is a legal value that must not be rejected. A blank pick is a real application state — audit_scoring.py has a regression asserting a blank G4 pick scores None rather than 0 or a crash — so a CHECK forbidding '' would refuse a state the app legitimately produces. Production holds 154 non-empty and zero empty today, which is exactly why the constraint must be argued from the app and not from the data.

indexes.rationale: one club per position per zone per entry — the natural key, and what makes the backfill idempotent
this entry's zone picks — the read the scoring path makes

addedEntitiesRationale.audit_event_details: NOT in the operator's list, but required by ratified decision B1. The hash chain must cover non-PII fields only, otherwise redacting PII for an erasure request breaks audit integrity. Splitting sensitive detail into an unchained sidecar is the mechanism that lets right-to-erasure and tamper-evidence coexist (G-02). Without it, B1 and G-02 are contradictory.

bolao.participant_state.why: active, merged away (superseded), or erased in place (redacted). No 'deleted' — participants are never deleted.

bolao.match_confidence.why: mirrors CONFIDENCE in identity.mjs; ordinal labels, never a numeric score, so no threshold can be automated

bolao.evidence_confidence.why: how a recorded fact is known. 'unknown' is a first-class value: a fee whose amount was never recorded must stay unknown

bolao.competition_kind.why: drives phase topology; the three shapes the platform's competitions actually take

bolao.edition_status.why: editions are retired by status, never deleted

bolao.pool_status.why: 'frozen' is the M13 read-only window and must be a first-class state, not a flag elsewhere

bolao.fee_basis.why: per_entry today; per_cota exists because cotas is already a modelled column

bolao.entry_state.why: withdrawal is a state plus deleted_at, never a row removal

bolao.settlement_status.why: mirrors SETTLEMENT in financial.mjs exactly. DERIVED_VIEW only — no table stores it. `unknown` means the EXPECTED FEE was never recorded, so no settlement claim is possible — distinct from legacy_asserted, which means the amount paid is unknown. Reporting such an entry as unpaid would fabricate a fee by implication.

bolao.payment_kind.why: the sign CHECK depends on this exact set; refund/reversal/chargeback are the negative-amount kinds. `adjustment` is declared but NOT implemented in financial_evidence.mjs PAYMENT_KIND, and is therefore unreachable: no code path produces it and no invariant governs its sign. Left in the enum deliberately rather than removed, because dropping an enum value is impossible once any row uses it — but it must not be written until the sign rule and reconciliation treatment are specified (BATCH-G-OP-2).

bolao.match_status.why: a finished match must have a result (DQ-PR-05); postponed and cancelled must not

bolao.outbox_status.why: mirrors STATUS in outbox.mjs. 'dead' is not terminal — replay returns it to pending

bolao.outbox_channel.why: email today; webhook declared because the outbox is channel-agnostic by design

bolao.delivery_outcome.why: mirrors OUTCOME in outbox.mjs; the transient/permanent split is what decides retry vs dead
